name: Oscar White
chief_complaint: Right ear pain and fever for 2 days
opening_statement: Hello doctor, Oscar has been pulling at his right ear and crying more than usual. He's had a fever since yesterday and didn't sleep well last night.
emotional_baseline: Irritable and uncomfortable, but consolable by parent. Moderate distress from ear pain.

rag_citations.citation: Ear pain is the cardinal symptom of AOM, often accompanied by fever and irritability in young children

rag_citations.source: eTG Acute Otitis Media - Clinical Features
rag_citations.citation: Fever >38°C is common in AOM but not universal; higher temperatures may indicate more severe infection
Decreased oral intake is common due to pain with sucking/swallowing in AOM

past_medical_history.notes: Full term delivery, normal developmental milestones, up-to-date immunisations per Australian National Immunisation Program

family_history: Non-contributory. No family history of immunodeficiency, chronic ear disease, or hearing loss.

social_history.living_situation: Lives with both parents and 5-year-old sibling
social_history.immunisation_status: Fully immunised per Australian schedule (13-valent pneumococcal vaccine at 2, 4, 6 months)

right_ear.tympanic_membrane: Bulging, erythematous, loss of light reflex, reduced mobility on pneumatic otoscopy

examination_findings.lymph_nodes: Small (<1cm) anterior cervical lymph nodes bilaterally, mobile, non-tender
examination_findings.chest: Clear breath sounds bilaterally, no wheeze or crackle

investigations.rationale: Clinical diagnosis of uncomplicated AOM. No investigations required unless treatment failure or complications suspected.

expected_management.action: Symptomatic management with regular paracetamol (15mg/kg every 4-6 hours) or ibuprofen (10mg/kg every 6-8 hours)

rag_citation.citation: Analgesia is essential in AOM management; regular paracetamol or ibuprofen recommended

expected_management.action: Watchful waiting (48-72 hours) is appropriate for uncomplicated AOM in child >6 months with mild symptoms
expected_management.pbs_restriction: Amoxicillin unrestricted on PBS if antibiotics required

rag_citation.source: eTG Acute Otitis Media - Antibiotic Use
rag_citation.citation: Delayed antibiotic prescription is appropriate for children >6 months with uncomplicated AOM and adequate follow-up

expected_management.action: Return if: fever persists >48 hours, symptoms worsen, ear discharge develops, or new symptoms (e.g., severe headache, neck stiffness, facial weakness)
Review in 48-72 hours (phone or in-person). If no improvement, commence amoxicillin 50mg/kg/day divided TDS for 5 days
Advise on pain management, fluid intake, identifying red flags. Avoid air travel if possible during acute phase.
expected_management.rationale: Empowers parents to manage at home and recognise complications

critical_errors.error: Prescribing immediate antibiotics without considering watchful waiting in uncomplicated AOM
critical_errors.consequence: Contributes to antimicrobial resistance; not evidence-based practice

critical_errors.error: Failing to provide adequate analgesia or discussing pain management
critical_errors.consequence: Unnecessary suffering; analgesia is cornerstone of AOM management

critical_errors.error: Not performing otoscopy or inadequate examination of tympanic membranes
critical_errors.consequence: Cannot confirm diagnosis; may miss bilateral disease or complications

critical_errors.error: Failing to provide safety-netting advice about complications (mastoiditis, meningitis)
critical_errors.consequence: Parents may not recognise serious deterioration requiring urgent care

critical_errors.error: Not asking about daycare attendance or smoke exposure
critical_errors.consequence: Misses modifiable risk factors for recurrent AOM

critical_errors.error: Not documenting tympanic membrane mobility on pneumatic otoscopy
critical_errors.consequence: Less accurate diagnosis; mobility assessment increases diagnostic certainty

fracp_reviews.comments: Excellent case for junior trainees. Accurately reflects current Australian guidelines (eTG) on watchful waiting vs immediate antibiotics. Parent presentation is realistic for this age group. Consider adding a question about breastfeeding history (protective factor).

Well-constructed case with appropriate difficulty level. The critical errors correctly identify common pitfalls (overprescribing antibiotics, inadequate analgesia). MBS/PBS references are accurate. Suggests good understanding of Australian primary care context.

learning_objectives.objective: Recognise clinical features of acute otitis media in preverbal children
Demonstrate competent otoscopic examination and interpretation of tympanic membrane findings
Apply evidence-based approach to antibiotic stewardship in uncomplicated AOM (watchful waiting)
Prescribe appropriate analgesia for paediatric patients using weight-based dosing
Provide effective safety-netting advice to parents about AOM complications
Identify modifiable risk factors for recurrent AOM (daycare, smoke exposure)
Navigate Australian primary care system (MBS items, PBS restrictions, eTG guidelines)
Distinguish uncomplicated AOM from cases requiring immediate antibiotics or specialist referral
